summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, and a history of Puestow procedure was admitted for severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Imaging revealed a partial small bowel obstruction without a clear transition point, along with a reducible ventral hernia. He was managed conservatively with NPO status, IV fluids, pain control, and manual hernia reduction. His psychiatric history, including depression and PTSD, was addressed with medication adjustments. By hospital day three, he tolerated a regular diet, remained pain-free, and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans. No surgical intervention was required.
